notes: Colloquial masculine تعبان (ta'ban) agrees with the speaker; feminine تعبانة (ta'bana). Form shared across Egyptian, Levantine, Gulf and Iraqi Arabic (MSA uses متعب).
Colloquial masculine مبسوط (mabsut); feminine مبسوطة (mabsuta). Common to Egyptian and Levantine Arabic.
Egyptian Arabic expresses 'I know' with the active participle: masculine عارف ('arif) agrees with the speaker; feminine عارفة ('arfa).
Colloquial feminine تعبانة (ta'bana) agrees with the speaker; masculine تعبان (ta'ban). Form shared across Egyptian, Levantine, Gulf and Iraqi Arabic.
Feminine active participle عارفة ('arfa) agrees with the speaker; masculine عارف ('arif).
Masculine تعبان agrees with the third-person subject هو (he), not the speaker; the speaker's gender is unknown.

glossEn: How are you doing? (asked of a woman)
notes: Standard Egyptian greeting; feminine active participle عاملة marks the ADDRESSEE, not the speaker (masculine addressee: عامل إيه؟).
